faq: Does Trip Campus plan tours for college groups?

Yes. Most Trip Campus packages are planned for college groups travelling from Kerala, with train or bus travel, stay, three meals a day, entry tickets and sightseeing arranged for the whole group. Family and friends groups can book the shorter Kerala trips too.
What is included in a Trip Campus package?

Rooms on a share basis, a tourist bus for the whole route, three unlimited meals a day (chicken is limited), all entry tickets, and toll, parking and taxes. Train packages include the train tickets. Camera fees inside monuments, travel insurance and personal expenses are not included.

Train packages start from Thrissur, Kuttippuram or Shornur railway stations. One Karnataka package starts with pickup at Mangalore railway station, and the Kerala hill trips leave by bus from your college. The boarding point can be fixed with each group.
How much does a package cost?
The price depends on the package, group size, travel dates and boarding point. Send your group details on WhatsApp or call and Trip Campus will share the itinerary and a quote.
Message Trip Campus on WhatsApp or call any of the numbers on this site with your group size and preferred month. Payment can be made by Google Pay or bank transfer.
Does Trip Campus offer other travel services?

Yes. Trip Campus Tourism is an IATA accredited agent and also books flights and hotels, arranges car rentals and travel insurance, and helps with visas, passports, certificate attestation and Hajj and Umrah travel.

destinations.name: Goa
destinations.when: November to February, when the sea is calm and the evenings are cool.
destinations.about: India's smallest state is a tropical coast of sun-kissed beaches, swaying palms and Portuguese heritage. Its 100-kilometre shoreline runs from busy Calangute and Baga to quiet Agonda and Palolem, with whitewashed churches, colourful markets and seafood in between. After sunset the beach shacks and clubs take over.
destinations.intro: For a college group, Goa is usually the last and most awaited stop of the trip. Trip Campus packages combine the churches and museum of Old Goa with the forts and beaches of North Goa, and the stay is in AC deluxe rooms on a share basis, close enough to the beaches for an evening out.
todo: Baga Beach and Tito's Lane after dark
Old Goa church and St Augustine Tower
Shopping before the night drive back
tips: Plan beach time for the late afternoon and evening, when the sun is softer.
Keep a change of clothes and a towel in the bus on beach days.
Old Goa's churches are places of worship, so dress modestly and keep noise low inside.
Stick to the group's meeting times at Baga and Calangute, where evenings get crowded.

destinations.name: Dandeli
destinations.when: October to February for river activities and forest walks.
destinations.about: A small town in the Western Ghats of Karnataka, surrounded by dense forest, rolling hills and the Kali River. The Dandeli Wildlife Sanctuary is home to the black panther and the Malabar pied hornbill, and the river is the place for rafting and kayaking. At night the forest comes alive with sound.
destinations.intro: Dandeli is the adventure day of the Karnataka trips. Groups arrive in the morning after an overnight drive, spend the day on the Kali River and in the forest, and end with a rain dance, DJ and campfire at the resort before moving on.
todo: Raft boating, kayaking and zorbing on the river
Hanging log, zig-zag bridge, quake walk and zip line
Rain dance with DJ and a campfire at the resort
tips: Wear quick-drying clothes and footwear that can get wet for rafting and kayaking.
Leave phones and wallets in the bus or a waterproof pouch during water activities.
Follow the instructors' safety briefing and keep life jackets on throughout.
Carry mosquito repellent for the evening at the forest resort.

destinations.name: Hampi
destinations.when: October to February. The ruins are open-air and summer days are very hot.
destinations.about: A UNESCO World Heritage Site on the banks of the Tungabhadra River, Hampi was once the capital of the Vijayanagara Empire. Today it is a landscape of ruins, temples and monuments among giant boulders, from the Virupaksha Temple to the Vittala Temple and the Royal Enclosure.
destinations.intro: Hampi is the history day of the Hampi, Dandeli and Goa tour. The ruins are spread over a wide area, so the group moves between the main sites by bus and on foot, from the Vittala temple complex in the morning to sunset over the boulders in the evening.
todo: Vijaya Vittala Temple and the Stone Chariot
Lotus Mahal and the Elephant Stable
tips: Start early: the stone and boulders get very hot by afternoon.
Wear comfortable walking shoes and a cap, and carry a water bottle.
Some temples ask visitors to remove footwear, so socks help on hot stone.
Keep to the group near the river and rocky viewpoints.

destinations.name: Lonavala
destinations.when: June to February. The hills are greenest in the monsoon.
destinations.about: A hill station in the Sahyadri range between Pune and Mumbai, known for old hill forts, rock-cut caves and viewpoints over deep valleys.
destinations.intro: Lonavala is the first hill stop of the Maharashtra tour, reached by road from Pune after the overnight train. The day mixes a hill fort, ancient rock-cut caves, a dam and valley viewpoints before the group stays the night in Lonavala.
tips: Lohagad Fort involves a climb of many steps, so wear shoes with good grip.
In the monsoon the paths can be slippery and misty; follow the guide closely.
Carry a light rain jacket between June and September.
Keep snacks and water for the fort climb.

destinations.name: Matheran
destinations.when: October to May for clear views from the points.
destinations.about: A small hill station in the Sahyadris where motor vehicles are not allowed. You go up from Aman Lodge, by toy train when it is running, and walk red-earth paths between the viewpoints.
destinations.intro: Matheran is a small hill station where motor vehicles are not allowed, so the group goes up from Aman Lodge by toy train when it is running, and walks between the viewpoints on red-earth paths. It is one of the quieter, greener days of the Maharashtra tour.
todo: Toy train from Aman Lodge (subject to availability)
King George Point, Malang Point and Lord Point
tips: Expect a lot of walking between points; comfortable shoes matter more than anywhere else on the trip.
The toy train depends on availability, so be ready for a walk or a short taxi from Aman Lodge.
Watch your belongings around the monkeys at viewpoints.
Keep together on the forest paths between points.

destinations.name: Mumbai
destinations.when: November to February, the cooler and drier months.
destinations.about: India's biggest city, built along the Arabian Sea. Two days cover the colonial landmarks of South Mumbai, the sea-facing promenades and a ferry out to the Elephanta Caves.
destinations.intro: Mumbai is the city finale of the Maharashtra tour. Two days cover South Mumbai's landmarks, the sea front at Marine Drive and Juhu, and the ferry to the Elephanta Caves for groups that choose it, before the night train back to Kerala from Panvel.
todo: Gateway of India and the Taj hotel
Bandra–Worli Sea Link and Juhu Beach
tips: Keep valuables secure in crowded places like Colaba Causeway and CST.
The Elephanta ferry is at your own cost; carry some cash for it.
Mumbai traffic is unpredictable, so be at the bus on time.
Try street food at Mohammed Ali Road as a group, and carry water.

destinations.name: Chikmagalur
destinations.when: September to March, when the peaks are clear and green.
destinations.about: Known as the coffee land of Karnataka, Chikmagalur is a hill station in the Western Ghats with trekking trails, coffee plantations, rivers and waterfalls. Mullayanagiri is the highest peak in Karnataka, and Baba Budangiri is a mountain range with pilgrimage sites.
destinations.intro: Chikmagalur is the hill day of the Chikmagalur packages. After an overnight drive, the group goes up by jeep to the highest viewpoints in Karnataka, with lunch at the hill station and stops at falls and viewpoints through the afternoon.
todo: Jeep ride up to Mullayanagiri Peak
tips: The peaks are windy and cool even in the dry months; carry a light jacket.
Jeep roads are rough, so carry tablets if you get travel sick.
Mullayanagiri has steps near the top; wear shoes with grip.
Mornings are clearest for photos from the peaks.

destinations.name: Gokarna
destinations.when: October to March, when the sea is calm.
destinations.about: A temple town on the Arabian Sea in Karnataka, where pilgrims and beach travellers share the same coast. The Mahabaleshwar Temple houses the Atmalinga of Lord Shiva, Om Beach is named for its shape and is the place to watch the sunset, and Kudle Beach is a short trek away.
destinations.intro: Gokarna is the beach stop of the Gokarna packages, quieter than Goa and known for its temple town and coves. Groups visit Om Beach and Kudle Beach for the sunset, with Yana Caves, Mirjan Fort or Murudeshwar on the way depending on the package.
todo: Mirjan Fort on the way in
tips: The paths between Gokarna's beaches are rocky; wear sandals with grip.
Do not swim beyond the safe area: currents can be strong.
The Mahabaleshwar Temple and Murudeshwar are places of worship; dress modestly.
Carry a cap and sunscreen for the afternoon on the beach.

destinations.name: Munnar
destinations.when: September to March for cool, clear days.
destinations.about: A hill station in Kerala known for its tea plantations, misty mountains and cool climate. The road winds through green tea gardens from one viewpoint to the next.
destinations.intro: Munnar is the first half of the Munnar and Vattavada trip. The group drives up overnight, sees the tea-garden viewpoints and Gap Road on the first morning, then spends the afternoon and evening at a resort with an infinity pool, games and a campfire.
todo: Infinity pool and games at the resort
tips: Nights are cold; carry a sweater, socks and a jacket.
The road to Munnar is winding, so carry travel-sickness tablets.
Gap Road viewpoints can be windy and misty; stay behind the barriers.
Carry swimwear for the resort pool.

destinations.name: Vattavada
destinations.when: September to March. Carry warm clothes for the evenings.
destinations.about: A farming village in the highlands near Munnar, surrounded by the Western Ghats. It is known for its cool climate, misty valleys, waterfalls and terraced vegetable and fruit farms.
destinations.intro: Vattavada is the second day of the Munnar trip, a farming village in the highlands near Munnar. The afternoon is a jeep trek to waterfalls, viewpoints and the terraced vegetable and fruit farms, with time to buy fresh produce before the drive back.
tips: The jeep track is bumpy; sit firmly and keep bags on your lap.
Evenings are cold, so keep a warm layer handy.
Ask before entering or photographing farms.
Carry a little cash for fresh fruit and vegetables.

destinations.name: Wayanad
destinations.when: October to May. Forest trails can close in heavy monsoon rain.
destinations.about: A green hill district in Kerala with forests, rolling hills and waterfalls. The trip climbs by jeep into the 900 Woods forest for a resort stay, and takes in Pookode Lake and the Banasura Sagar Dam.
destinations.intro: Wayanad is a short forest getaway. The highlight is a jeep safari up to the 900 Woods area for a resort night with a pool, forest trekking and a campfire, with Lakkidi viewpoint, a tribal village visit, Pookode Lake and Banasura Sagar Dam on either side.
todo: Forest trekking, pool and campfire at the resort
Pookode Lake, Banasura Sagar Dam and Karapuzha park
tips: Carry a jacket: nights in the forest are cool.
Wear closed shoes for the forest trek and carry leech socks in the wet months.
The glass bridge is optional and has its own rules; check before joining.
Respect the people and customs at En Ooru tribal village.

destinations.name: Ramakkalmedu
destinations.when: September to March for clear views and steady wind on the ridge.
destinations.about: A hill station in Idukki, Kerala, at about 3,500 feet, with wide views over the mountains, valleys and villages below. Windmills line the ridge and the sunset turns the sky gold and crimson.
destinations.intro: Ramakkalmedu is a windy ridge in Idukki on the Kerala and Tamil Nadu border. The group spends a full day there: a jeep safari to Amappara and the caves in the morning, a walking trek after lunch, sunset from the ridge and a campfire with DJ at night.
todo: Jeep safari to Amappara and its caves
tips: It is very windy on the ridge; hold on to caps and phones.
Wear shoes with grip for the rocky viewpoints and caves.
Stay well back from cliff edges at the viewpoints.
Carry a warm layer for the campfire night.

destinations.name: Kodaikanal
destinations.when: October to June. Carry warm clothes all year.
destinations.about: A hill station in the Palani hills of Tamil Nadu, called the Princess of Hill Stations. It is built around the star-shaped Kodai Lake, with valleys, tall cliffs and pine forest around it.
destinations.intro: Kodaikanal is the second day of the Ramakkalmedu trip. The group drives across to Tamil Nadu in the morning, passing the Cumbum and Theni grape farms if time allows, and covers the main viewpoints, caves and forest in the afternoon before an evening at Kodai Lake.
tips: Carry a sweater or jacket: it is cool all year.
Viewpoints like Pillar Rocks can be covered in mist; be patient for the view.
Stay on marked paths at Guna Caves and cliff viewpoints.
Kodai Lake's market is good for chocolates and souvenirs.

iv.title: IV Packages from Kerala – Industrial Visit & Study Tours
iv.desc: IV (industrial visit) and study tour packages from Kerala for colleges: 3 to 6 day trips by train or bus, with stay, meals and tickets included.
iv.h1: IV and study tour packages from Kerala
iv.lead: In Kerala colleges the class trip is often called an IV (industrial visit) or a study tour. Trip Campus plans these trips for departments and classes from start to finish: train or tourist bus, rooms, three meals a day, entry tickets and sightseeing.
why: Packages are built around class trips, with 21 to 49-seat tourist buses depending on the size of the group.
Train tickets or a tourist bus for the whole route, rooms on a share basis, meals and entry tickets are arranged before you leave.
Every package has a full itinerary, so you can share it with your department and parents before the trip.
Plan everything with Trip Campus on WhatsApp or a call, from the first quote to the return journey.
faqs: IV stands for industrial visit. In many Kerala colleges the term is used for the department or class tour, which usually combines travel and sightseeing over 3 to 6 days. Some courses also include a visit to a company or institution.
Can a company or institution visit be added to the IV?
Tell Trip Campus which kind of visit your department needs and on which route. Trip Campus will tell you whether it can be fitted into the plan.
Which packages are best for an IV or study tour?

For 5 to 6 days, the Karnataka and Goa train tours (Dandeli and Goa, Hampi, Dandeli and Goa, or Chikmagalur, Dandeli and Goa) and Lonavala, Matheran and Mumbai are the most complete. For a shorter trip, Dandeli and Gokarna takes 4 days, and the Kerala hill trips take 3.
Each student should carry a college ID card and a government photo ID. Your college may also ask for a permission letter and parent consent before the trip.
How is the price worked out?
The price depends on the package, the number of students, travel dates and the boarding point. Send your group details on WhatsApp for a quote.
Ask Trip Campus when you request a quote; staff arrangements are agreed with each group.

checklist: Fix the dates early
Agree on the month with your department first. Train-based tours need tickets booked well ahead, and popular months fill quickly.
Count the group
Get a firm number of students and staff. Group size decides the bus size, rooms and the price per head.
Choose the trip length
3 days suits the Kerala hill trips; 4 to 6 days covers Karnataka, Goa or Maharashtra by train.
Get permissions
Most colleges need a permission letter from the principal and consent from parents. Start this as soon as the dates are fixed.
Ask for a full itinerary and quote
Share group size, month and boarding point with the tour operator. Check what is included: transport, rooms, meals, entry tickets, toll and parking.
Check what is not included
Camera fees at monuments, travel insurance, optional activities and personal expenses are usually extra.
Collect ID details
Train tickets and hotels need names and ages, and everyone should carry a college ID and a government photo ID.
Share the plan
Send the day-by-day plan, emergency numbers and packing list to students and parents before the trip.
Pack right
Medicines for travel sickness, headache and cold; caps; ID cards; warm clothes for hill stations; quick-dry clothes for river activities.
Keep to time on the trip
Most of a tour's plan depends on the group being on the bus on time. Agree on a meeting rule before you leave.
